unit: P6 flash-vram-attribution (numerics write-owner close-out of the BLOCK 1/2/3 audit's peak-VRAM regression finding)
method:
Attribution: crates/jammi-encoders/src/modernbert.rs's modernbert::tests::flash_vs_block_per_layer_vram_attribution_probe_cuda -- cudarc::driver::result::mem_get_info() after each layer's forward and after backward, both arms, one process, same loaded checkpoint (batch=8, seq=512, seed=42, bf16). Found: the two-op flash composition (RopePositionsFused producing a rotated qkv Tensor, then flash_attention_varlen consuming it) retains a SECOND [total,3,H,64] bf16 buffer per layer (~24-28 MiB observed, ~24.0 MiB (25.17 MB) predicted from shape) that the block arm never pays -- candle's BackpropOp::new1 (op.rs) clones flash_attention_varlen's own `arg` (the ALREADY-rotated qkv) into its Op node unconditionally, and that rotated buffer is a fresh allocation distinct from the pre-rotation qkv the Wqkv linear's own backward needs anyway (which both arms retain equally). The block arm (AttentionBlockFused) avoids this because it fuses RoPE INSIDE its own CustomOp3 and recomputes the rotation from the pre-rotation qkv in a DETACHED bwd, never materializing a separately-retained rotated buffer. dq_accum (20.97 MB, FlashVarlenBwdHelper's own backward scratch) is CONFIRMED NOT the cause -- it is freed within the same backward call, not sustained.

Fix: FlashVarlenAttentionFusedRope (crates/jammi-kernels/src/ops/flash_attention.rs), a new CustomOp3 over (qkv, cos, sin) fusing RopePositionsFused's row math with flash_attention_varlen's own FFI calls inside ONE op -- forward calls the exact same underlying functions (crate::cuda::rope_positions::cuda_fwd then flash::flash_varlen_fwd_into) the two-op composition calls, in the same order; bwd recomputes the rotation from the (already-alive, detached) pre-rotation qkv via RopePositionsFused directly, mirroring AttentionBlockFused's own 'recompute in a DETACHED bwd' idiom, instead of letting candle's tape retain a rotated buffer for the whole backward pass. Proven bit-identical to the two-op composition it replaces, forward AND backward, in ops::flash_attention::fused_rope_matches_two_op_composition::fused_rope_matches_two_op_composition_bit_identical_fwd_and_bwd_cuda.

per_layer_vram_probe.note: modernbert::tests::flash_vs_block_per_layer_vram_attribution_probe_cuda's own --nocapture output, attention+MLP layers only (no optimizer, no LoRA epilogue outside the layer stack) -- a SUBSET of a full finetune-step, isolating the attention arm as the sole source of any difference (MLP is identical code on both arms). Absolute free-memory readings via cuMemGetInfo_v2 after a device sync; 'total consumed' = start free - after-backward free, within ONE run (controls for cross-run allocator drift -- see the flash/block gap column, which is comparable across the two runs below even though each run's own absolute numbers are not, because of exactly that drift).
per_layer_vram_probe.caveat: the block arm's own absolute numbers drift ~192 MiB between the two runs (unchanged code, same seed) -- ordinary cudarc/CUDA-allocator fragmentation noise at this granularity (candidate (4) in the dispatch, confirmed present but small relative to the ~2.5 GB full-step regression this closes). The flash/block GAP (not the absolute numbers) is the controlled comparison.

flash_arm.s_per_step_note: no meaningful change (expected -- this fix changes RETENTION, not the compute this op issues; the difference is within ordinary run-to-run noise).

block_arm_baseline_unchanged_code.note: unchanged code path (JAMMI_KERNELS_DISABLE=attention_block_flash forces the block arm on both builds) -- the +0.7% drift between before/after means is the SAME allocator-fragmentation noise the per-layer probe's own caveat names, not a code effect.

flash_minus_block_gap.interpretation: BEFORE: flash's peak VRAM exceeded the block arm's by 2.40 GB -- the anomaly this round closes (the lead's own arithmetic: flash SHOULD save MORE than block, since flash never materializes the block arm's [b,h,s,s] bf16 probability tensor, ~67 MB/layer). AFTER: flash's peak VRAM is 0.20 GB BELOW the block arm's -- the sign has flipped to the theoretically-expected direction. The gap is not fully eliminated to the full ~1.8 GB theoretical block-arm-probability-tensor saving (dq_accum's 20.97 MB backward scratch and ordinary allocator fragmentation, both confirmed present and both un-owned-by-jammi, account for the remainder plausibly, but were not further decomposed this round -- see 'what remains' below).

expected_dispatch_identity: attention_block_flash.fused == 28 * forwards_per_step(1, batched) * (warmup+steps=30) == 840 on every flash-on leg; attention_block_flash.declined == 840 and attention_block_fused == 840 on every flash-off (DISABLE) leg -- checked directly off each raw run's own dispatch counters, all 8 runs above match this identity.

gate_outcomes_this_session.cargo test -p jammi-kernels -p jammi-enc: PASS 308 + 132, incl. fused_rope_matches_two_op_composition_bit_identical_fwd_and_bwd_cuda, flash_vs_block_per_layer_vram_attribution_probe_cuda, flash_arm_encoder_level_three_way_oracle_dense_cuda_bf16, and all three RED controls (flash_arm_encoder_level_oracle_red_control_{bad_softmax_scale,k_unrotated,window_dropped})
gate_outcomes_this_session.RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p ja: PASS (one round: a public-fn doc comment linked a crate-private type and an out-of-scope bare bracket link -- fixed by converting to a backtick code span / a fully-qualified super:: link, never a doc-hidden bypass, per 7fd457e's precedent)

what_remains: the FusedAttentionMasks::build reordering (build only when the block arm will actually run, flash decision first) is NOT done this round -- disclosed as deferred in the fix commit, not silently dropped. Its VRAM cost is small (a few MB, built once per forward) relative to the ~2.5 GB this round closes. The residual after-fix flash/block gap (-0.20 GB, i.e. flash now slightly BELOW block, not the full ~1.8 GB theoretical saving) was not further decomposed between dq_accum's backward scratch and ordinary allocator fragmentation -- both are named candidates in the dispatch, neither is jammi's own wiring, and the SIGN is now correct.
